item.statement: The relationship between the decomposition of the B2 phase into a two-phase B2 + BCC microstructure and the resulting coercivity is not well understood in these alloy systems.
quotes: The relationship between the decomposition of the B2 phase into a two-phase B2 + BCC microstructure and the resulting coercivity is not well understood in these alloy systems and requires further detailed investigation.

The details of the thermodynamic basis underlying the influence of Cr on phase separation in these complex concentrated multi-component alloys requires further analysis beyond the scope of the present paper.

Therefore, the role of Cr, an anti-ferromagnetic element, on the microstructural evolution and properties (magnetic and mechanical) of AlCo x Cr 1−x FeNi type HEAs, needs further investigation and forms the basis of the present study.

item.statement: The thermodynamic model predicted the formation of an FCC phase in the AlCoFeNi alloy at 1000 °C, but this phase was not observed experimentally.
quotes: Our experimental investigations match very well with the thermodynamic predictions, except for the FCC phase predicted in AlCoFeNi alloy at 1000 °C.
Note that there is likely to be a high thermodynamic nucleation barrier for the precipitation of the FCC phase within the B2 matrix owing to the high interfacial energy between these two phases.
However, in the experimental observations, there was no conclusive FCC formation observed in case of the AlCoFeNi 1000 °C/15 h annealed sample.

item.statement: Adding Cr improves corrosion resistance but is detrimental to soft magnetic properties by reducing saturation magnetization and increasing coercivity.
quotes: However, though Cr is detrimental to the soft magnetic properties, this alloying addition has beneficial effects in terms of other properties such as corrosion resistance.
The saturation magnetization of the AlCo 0.5 Cr 0.5 FeNi HEA reduces by more than 50% compared to samples with no Cr (AlCoFeNi).
Additionally, it is shown that replacement of Co by Cr in the AlCoFeNi alloy resulted in a substantial reduction in saturation magnetization and increase in coercivity.

item.statement: The thermodynamic basis for how Cr promotes phase separation in these complex multi-component alloys requires deeper analysis beyond the current scope.
quotes: The details of the thermodynamic basis underlying the influence of Cr on phase separation in these complex concentrated multi-component alloys requires further analysis beyond the scope of the present paper.
The strong tendency of Cr to introduce phase separation in the B2 phase can possibly be attributed to a positive enthalpy of mixing of Fe-Cr, Co-Cr and Ni-Cr systems.
Nevertheless, the importance of Cr in promoting phase separation in these HEAs needs to be recognized.

item.statement: Dark-field TEM imaging could not definitively distinguish between precipitates and strain contrast within the B2 matrix for the AlCoFeNi alloy annealed at 600 °C.
quotes: While this DFTEM image does exhibit some contrast with particle-like features, it is not possible to definitively attribute the contrast to precipitates, rather than simply strain contrast within the continuous B2 matrix.
This DFTEM image appears to be nearly identical to the one observed in case of the 1000 °C/15 h annealed sample, shown in Fig. 2(b).
Therefore, it is not possible to establish phase separation within the B2 matrix based on this dark-field image.

item.statement: Lower annealing temperatures (600 °C) lead to hierarchical phase decomposition which increases microhardness but significantly alters magnetic properties compared to the single-phase state.
quotes: This decomposition leads to a substantially higher microhardness coupled with a decrease in saturation magnetization ( M S ) and increase in coercivity ( H C ).

The lowest microhardness value of 406 VHN was observed for the AlCoFeNi alloy annealed at 1000 °C, while the highest microhardness value of 475 VHN was observed in case of the AlCo 0.5 Cr 0.5 FeNi alloy annealed at 600 °C.

The coercivity ( H c ) decreased with increasing annealing temperature from 15 Oe for sample aged at 600 °C/15 h, exhibiting nanoscale phase separation, to 4 Oe for samples aged at 1000 °C/15 h, exhibiting a homogeneous undecomposed B2 matrix.

item.statement: The specific thermodynamic interactions causing Cr to induce phase separation in these complex alloys need further analysis.
quotes: The details of the thermodynamic basis underlying the influence of Cr on phase separation in these complex concentrated multi-component alloys requires further analysis beyond the scope of the present paper.
The strong tendency of Cr to introduce phase separation in the B2 phase can possibly be attributed to a positive enthalpy of mixing of Fe-Cr, Co-Cr and Ni-Cr systems.
In all, it appears that the phase separation tendency in the current HEA is introduced by Cr.
